finding.claim: Unauthenticated OS command injection in GET /ping: the attacker-controlled query parameter `host` is concatenated into a shell command string and executed via child_process.exec, which runs it through /bin/sh. Shell metacharacters (e.g. `;`, `&&`, `|`, `$(...)`) in `host` run arbitrary commands as the server process user.
finding.source: tools.js:6-7 — `req.query.host` from the HTTP query string (attacker-controlled, no validation).
finding.sink: tools.js:7 — `exec("ping -c 1 " + req.query.host, ...)`, which spawns a shell and executes the concatenated string.

trace.note: app.get("/ping") route registered; no auth middleware on the app or route.
req.query.host read and concatenated into the command string with no quoting, escaping, or allowlist.
child_process.exec passes the full string to /bin/sh -c, so injected metacharacters create new commands.
app.listen(3001) exposes the route on all interfaces by default, making it reachable by any network client.

finding.guards_checked: No input validation or type check on req.query.host (Express may yield string, array, or nested object; all still concatenate into the shell string). No use of execFile/argv-array (the safe form) for this route. No authentication or authorization middleware. Decoy 28 (shell=True with only closed-map or integer fragments) does NOT apply: the fragment is raw user input, not a constant or coerced integer. Non-findings checked: /version uses execFile with constant argv and no user input; /uptime runs a constant string with exec but no user input.

verdict.reason: tools.js:7 concatenates the raw query parameter `req.query.host` into a string passed to child_process.exec, which runs it through /bin/sh, and tools.js:6 registers the route with no auth middleware, while tools.js:28 `app.listen(3001)` binds on all interfaces by default, so any anonymous network client can inject shell metacharacters.
